    n=min(20_000, len(steam)),
    random_state=42,
)

x = plot_data["price"]
y = plot_data["positive_ratio"]

slope, intercept = np.polyfit(
    x,
    y,
    1,
)

x_line = np.linspace(
    x.min(),
    x.max(),
    200,
)

point_sizes = (
    np.log1p(
        plot_data["total_ratings"]
    )
    * 3
)


fig, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(9, 6)
)

ax.scatter(
    x,
    y,
    s=point_sizes,
    alpha=0.15,
)

ax.plot(
    x_line,
    slope * x_line + intercept,
    linewidth=2,
)

ax.set_title(
    "Game Price and Positive Review Ratio"
)

ax.set_xlabel(
    "Game Price"
)

ax.set_ylabel(
    "Positive Review Ratio"
)

ax.set_ylim(0, 1)

ax.text(
    0.03,
    0.96,
    (
        f"Pearson r = {corr:.3f}\n"
        f"p = {p_value:.3g}"
    ),
    transform=ax.transAxes,
    va="top",
)

ax.text(
    0.97,
    0.04,
    "Point size reflects\ntotal rating volume",
    transform=ax.transAxes,
    ha="right",
    va="bottom",
    fontsize=9,
)

plt.show()</cell id="6064034f">

Yes — the dataset only has `positive_ratings` and `negative_ratings` counts (no star/numeric score column). That reflects how Steam reviews actually work: each user review is a binary thumbs-up/thumbs-down ("Recommended"/"Not Recommended"), not a 1–5 or 1–10 scale.

So `positive_ratio` in the notebook is really "% of reviews that were thumbs-up," not an average of a graded rating — worth keeping in mind when interpreting the correlation with price.
